observations: A large rounded form fills most of the canvas, outlined in white against a green diamond-patterned background; the jaw extends downward and leftward, ending in a blunt curved point.

Two eye zones sit asymmetrically: the left is a dark recessed socket with a small orange ring; the right is more open, showing a red-and-white starburst ring on a dark field, with dense scribbled lines layered over both.

A wide mouth near the lower center shows a row of white rectangular teeth set against black, with a protruding lower-lip shape; the surface is covered in overlapping short scribble lines in yellow, cyan, red, and white.
reading: The form leans slightly left, its asymmetric eye sockets giving it an off-balance quality. One eye recedes into shadow while the other opens onto a red starburst, so the two sides carry different visual weights. The bared teeth read as a grin or a grimace depending on where attention lands first. Dense scribble lines across the surface sit inside a smooth white outer edge, holding the agitation in.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nifty faces #94 and nnxyz nifty faces #96. Where #94 uses a near-black field with sharp angular forms, and #96 uses flat orange with rigid rectangular geometry, this piece offers warm ochre curves on a patterned green ground.

connections.reason: Both works show a wide tooth-filled mouth as a dominant feature, but #96 renders it with hard rectangular outlines on a flat orange field while #95 wraps it in curved organic forms and layered scribble lines, making the contrast in edge quality concrete.
nnotb #162 also places two visually distinct eye zones on a single face and uses a comparable density of overlapping scribble lines, though its field is olive-gold and its outer forms are squarer.

interpretiveTags: dual visual weight within single form
lookingQuestion: The two eye zones are built from different shapes and colors — what does following the line from one eye across to the other reveal about how the face holds together?
ambiguities: The title number 95 does not confirm this is the ninety-fifth work made by the artist across any catalogue; title order and creation order are distinct.
QmNeEu68NZBuf2fuwo1mRN87Lo1m1jej1fumNyEZytvZV2 (nifty faces #94) was inspected but offers mainly contrast rather than a meaningful formal parallel, so it was not selected as a connection.
